newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP SAYS PETROLEUM CHIEF O'CONNOR RESIGNS.
newsitem.headline: BHP SAYS PETROLEUM CHIEF O'CONNOR RESIGNS.

text.p: The Broken Hill Proprietary Co Pty Ltd, Australia's largest listed company, said on Friday that BHP Petroleum chief John O'Connor has resigned because of irreconcilable differences between himself and the board.
BHP also said its board had unanimously confirmed its support for managing director John Prescott and for the business strategies being pursued by senior management.
BHP said Philip Aiken, the executive general manager of corporate development, would be acting executive general manager for the petroleum division for the present time.
O'Connor was reported in some newspapers this week as having promoted the float of the profitable petroleum division during briefings with analysts in Sydney and Melbourne.
A float is believed to have been rejected by the company in the past as part of the wide-ranging strategy led by Prescott to examine all divisions and improve BHP's operating performance.

"The board has unanimously confirmed its support for John Prescott as the managing director, for the business strategies being pursued by the senior management of the company, and for the progress being made. There is absolutely no dissension on this point," chairman Jerry Ellis said in a statement.
O'Connor's resignation brings to three the number of senior executives who have resigned or retired in the last three days.
